title_text: Finite Unambiguity is Not Equivalent to Unambiguity

Paragraph.Text: For a while I believed finite unambiguity to be equivalent to the other definitions of unambiguity.
We may use an analogy from the category of sets, however I had missed the infinite case when translating this idea to grammars.

It is true that if a grammar is unambiguous, then it is finitely unambiguous. However, the converse does not hold unless the grammar has finitely many parse trees for each string.
